lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: checking safety and supervision

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 6 — family contribution capstone
objective: Learners take their own step list from the previous lesson and check each step against three specific hazard categories — heat, a sharp tool, and a chemical cleaner — marking every step with one of three labels: adult right there, adult checking in partway through, or learner alone, so the plan is ready for a guardian's first look before any part of the job actually happens.
scenario: Sitting with the step list from day two, the learner goes through it one step at a time and asks the same question for every step: does this step involve heat, a sharp tool, or a chemical cleaner, or does it happen somewhere no one else can see. The learner writes one of three labels next to each step, then shows the marked-up list to a guardian for a first look, without doing any part of the job itself yet.
safetyNotes: This lesson is a planning discussion only; the learner does not use heat, sharp tools, or a chemical cleaner during this lesson.
If any step on the list is unclear, the safe choice is to label it 'adult right there' rather than guess, and that caution counts as success.
materials: the step list from the previous lesson
a pencil or marker for labeling

tasks.directions: Before marking anything, reread your step list from the previous lesson start to finish.

prompts.text: Name one step on your list that you are already fairly sure would need an adult nearby, and say why.

tasks.directions: Go through your step list one step at a time and mark each step adult right there, adult checking in, or learner alone, based on whether it involves heat, a sharp tool, or a chemical cleaner.

prompts.text: I checked every step on my list, not just the ones that looked risky at first glance.
I used the three specific hazard checks (heat, sharp tool, chemical cleaner) instead of just guessing which steps felt risky.
I wrote one label (adult right there, adult checking in, or learner alone) next to every step.
I showed my marked-up list to a guardian and listened to anything they wanted to add or change.

tasks.directions: Without any more help, decide on one overall plan for supervision.

prompts.text: Looking at your marked-up list, write one sentence describing what kind of adult supervision your whole job will need overall, using your step labels as evidence.

tasks.directions: Think about whether any step surprised you once you applied the checks.

prompts.text: Was there a step you first thought was safe alone but labeled differently after checking the three hazards? Describe the step and what changed your mind.

remediation: If a learner marks every step 'learner alone' without applying the three specific hazard checks, reteach with two contrasting example steps side by side, one with a clear hazard and one without, and have the learner state out loud which of the three checks applies before marking either one.
extension: Have the learner pick one step marked 'adult right there' and write a second, safer version of that same step that could be marked 'learner alone' instead, if a safer version exists.
